context:
First make the critical section explicit: only one process should decide and
populate a shared archive path at a time. Then switch the downloader to a
process-unique temporary path plus atomic replace, so the final path is
either absent or checksum-verified. Keep the implementation generic in
`data_fetch`, not JoinOrder-specific.
description:
Housekeeping for the JoinOrder canonical cutover audited
`benchbox/core/data_fetch/` and found that archive downloads are not guarded
against concurrent callers writing the same destination file.

`fetch_data()` resolves the archive path under the benchmark output
directory and calls `download(manifest.url, archive_path, ...)` when table
files are missing. `download()` writes directly to `dest_path`, resumes from
existing bytes with a Range request, and verifies the final checksum. There is
no per-archive lock, no unique `.part` path per process, and no atomic
`os.replace()` from a completed temp file. Two processes that start with a
missing archive can therefore append/truncate the same file concurrently and
either corrupt the archive or waste a large download before checksum failure.

This affects every benchmark that uses `benchbox/core/data_fetch/`, not just
JoinOrder, so the housekeeping TODO deliberately records it as a separate
follow-up instead of fixing it inline.
